dialogue.text: The world will never be the same.
dialogue.zh: 世界將永遠改變。
dialogue.ja: 世界は二度と同じにはならない。
dialogue.local: The world will never be the same.
dialogue.en: The world will never be the same.

dialogue.text: In the closing years of the 19th century, the world was entering the Electric Revolution.
dialogue.zh: 在19世紀末，世界正進入電氣革命。
dialogue.ja: 19世紀の終わり頃、世界は電気革命の時代に入ろうとしていた。
dialogue.local: In the closing years of the 19th century, the world was entering the Electric Revolution.
dialogue.en: In the closing years of the 19th century, the world was entering the Electric Revolution.

dialogue.text: In the United States, a fierce contest raged over Electric Power Transmission.
dialogue.zh: 在美國，關於電力傳輸展開了激烈的競爭。
dialogue.ja: アメリカでは、電力送電を巡って激しい争いが繰り広げられていた。
dialogue.local: In the United States, a fierce contest raged over Electric Power Transmission.
dialogue.en: In the United States, a fierce contest raged over Electric Power Transmission.

dialogue.text: The War of the Currents.
dialogue.zh: 電流之戰。
dialogue.ja: 電流戦争。
dialogue.local: The War of the Currents.
dialogue.en: The War of the Currents.

dialogue.text: On one side, Thomas Edison advocated direct current, or DC.
dialogue.zh: 一方，托馬斯·愛迪生主張直流電，簡稱DC。
dialogue.ja: 一方では、トーマス・エジソンが直流電流（DC）を支持していた。
dialogue.local: On one side, Thomas Edison advocated direct current, or DC.
dialogue.en: On one side, Thomas Edison advocated direct current, or DC.

dialogue.text: On the other, Nikola Tesla and George Westinghouse promoted alternating current, or AC,
dialogue.zh: 另一方，尼古拉·特斯拉和喬治·威斯汀豪斯推廣交流電，簡稱AC，
dialogue.ja: 他方では、ニコラ・テスラとジョージ・ウェスティングハウスが交流電流（AC）を推進していた。
dialogue.local: On the other, Nikola Tesla and George Westinghouse promoted alternating current, or AC,
dialogue.en: On the other, Nikola Tesla and George Westinghouse promoted alternating current, or AC,

dialogue.text: which could travel long distances more efficiently, and was far less hazardous over high-voltage lines.
dialogue.zh: 交流電能更有效地傳輸長距離，且在高壓線路上更安全。
dialogue.ja: 交流電は長距離をより効率的に送電でき、高電圧の送電線でもはるかに安全だった。
dialogue.local: which could travel long distances more efficiently, and was far less hazardous over high-voltage lines.
dialogue.en: which could travel long distances more efficiently, and was far less hazardous over high-voltage lines.

dialogue.text: By the dawn of the 20th century, AC had prevailed, lighting modern cities worldwide.
dialogue.zh: 到了20世紀初，交流電勝出，照亮了全球現代城市。
dialogue.ja: 20世紀の幕開けには、交流電が勝利し、世界中の現代都市を照らした。
dialogue.local: By the dawn of the 20th century, AC had prevailed, lighting modern cities worldwide.
dialogue.en: By the dawn of the 20th century, AC had prevailed, lighting modern cities worldwide.

dialogue.text: Although Edison didn't win that battle, his work on the Electric Light bulb led to an unexpected discovery, one that would ultimately pave the way for the electronics of the future.
dialogue.zh: 雖然愛迪生未贏得那場戰爭，但他在電燈泡上的研究帶來了意想不到的發現，最終為未來電子學鋪路。
dialogue.ja: エジソンはその戦いに勝てなかったが、電球の研究が予期せぬ発見をもたらし、未来の電子工学への道を開いた。
dialogue.local: Although Edison didn't win that battle, his work on the Electric Light bulb led to an unexpected discovery, one that would ultimately pave the way for the electronics of the future.
dialogue.en: Although Edison didn't win that battle, his work on the Electric Light bulb led to an unexpected discovery, one that would ultimately pave the way for the electronics of the future.

dialogue.text: Out of Edison's humble incandescent lamps appeared a strange phenomenon.
dialogue.zh: 在愛迪生簡單的白熾燈泡中出現了一種奇特現象。
dialogue.ja: エジソンの質素な白熱電球から奇妙な現象が現れた。
dialogue.local: Out of Edison's humble incandescent lamps appeared a strange phenomenon.
dialogue.en: Out of Edison's humble incandescent lamps appeared a strange phenomenon.

dialogue.text: When the filament was heated white hot with direct current, the bulbs interior eventually darkened on one side, as tiny particles from the filament deposited on the glass.
dialogue.zh: 當燈絲用直流電加熱至白熱時，燈泡內部一側逐漸變暗，因為燈絲上的微小粒子沉積在玻璃上。
dialogue.ja: フィラメントが直流電で白熱すると、電球の内側の一方が暗くなり、フィラメントからの微粒子がガラスに付着したためだった。
dialogue.local: When the filament was heated white hot with direct current, the bulbs interior eventually darkened on one side, as tiny particles from the filament deposited on the glass.
dialogue.en: When the filament was heated white hot with direct current, the bulbs interior eventually darkened on one side, as tiny particles from the filament deposited on the glass.

dialogue.text: Working to address it, Edison observed that a current could pass through a partial vacuum from the hot filament to a nearby metal plate, an effect he filed a patent for in 1883.
dialogue.zh: 為了解決這問題，愛迪生發現電流能穿過部分真空，從熱燈絲流向附近的金屬板，並於1883年申請了專利。
dialogue.ja: この問題に取り組む中で、エジソンは熱いフィラメントから近くの金属板へ部分真空を通じて電流が流れることを観察し、1883年に特許を申請した。
dialogue.local: Working to address it, Edison observed that a current could pass through a partial vacuum from the hot filament to a nearby metal plate, an effect he filed a patent for in 1883.
dialogue.en: Working to address it, Edison observed that a current could pass through a partial vacuum from the hot filament to a nearby metal plate, an effect he filed a patent for in 1883.

dialogue.text: Want broad claims on using the current give us that by heated vacuum lamps for this purpose and other purposes?
dialogue.zh: 他申請了廣泛的專利權，涵蓋利用加熱真空燈泡中電流的各種用途。
dialogue.ja: 彼はこの電流を利用するための幅広い特許請求を行い、この目的やその他の用途に使う加熱真空ランプに関するものだった。
dialogue.local: Want broad claims on using the current give us that by heated vacuum lamps for this purpose and other purposes?
dialogue.en: Want broad claims on using the current give us that by heated vacuum lamps for this purpose and other purposes?

dialogue.text: Later known as the Edison effect, though he could not foresee its destiny.
dialogue.zh: 後來被稱為愛迪生效應，但他無法預見它的未來命運。
dialogue.ja: 後にエジソン効果と呼ばれたが、彼はその運命を予見できなかった。
dialogue.local: Later known as the Edison effect, though he could not foresee its destiny.
dialogue.en: Later known as the Edison effect, though he could not foresee its destiny.

dialogue.text: I have just completed a pressure indicator which works perfectly.
dialogue.zh: 我剛完成了一個運作完美的壓力指示器。
dialogue.ja: 私はちょうど完璧に動作する圧力計を完成させたところだ。
dialogue.local: I have just completed a pressure indicator which works perfectly.
dialogue.en: I have just completed a pressure indicator which works perfectly.

dialogue.text: Following this discovery, engineers began experimenting with the plate's placement and designed to better capture the particles and prevent the darkening.
dialogue.zh: 在這項發現後，工程師開始試驗金屬板的位置，設計以更好地捕捉粒子並防止變暗。
dialogue.ja: この発見を受けて、技術者たちは金属板の配置を試行し、粒子をよりよく捕らえ暗くなるのを防ぐ設計を始めた。
dialogue.local: Following this discovery, engineers began experimenting with the plate's placement and designed to better capture the particles and prevent the darkening.
dialogue.en: Following this discovery, engineers began experimenting with the plate's placement and designed to better capture the particles and prevent the darkening.

dialogue.text: This laid the groundwork for the vacuum tube era.
dialogue.zh: 這為真空管時代奠定了基礎。
dialogue.ja: これが真空管時代の基盤を築いた。
dialogue.local: This laid the groundwork for the vacuum tube era.
dialogue.en: This laid the groundwork for the vacuum tube era.

dialogue.text: In 1906, leader forest added a third electrode, the grid, inventing the triode, the first vacuum tube capable of amplifying electrical signals.
dialogue.zh: 1906年，李德福斯特加入第三個電極——柵極，發明了三極管，首個能放大電信號的真空管。
dialogue.ja: 1906年、リーダー・フォレストは第三の電極であるグリッドを加え、電気信号を増幅できる最初の真空管、トライオードを発明した。
dialogue.local: In 1906, leader forest added a third electrode, the grid, inventing the triode, the first vacuum tube capable of amplifying electrical signals.
dialogue.en: In 1906, leader forest added a third electrode, the grid, inventing the triode, the first vacuum tube capable of amplifying electrical signals.

dialogue.text: By placing a wire mesh grid between the heated cathode and the plate, he could control the flow of electricity, turning faint currents into strong, usable signals.
dialogue.zh: 他在加熱的陰極與金屬板之間放置了金屬網柵，能控制電流流動，將微弱電流轉為強大且可用的信號。
dialogue.ja: 加熱された陰極とプレートの間にワイヤーメッシュのグリッドを置くことで、微弱な電流を強力で使いやすい信号に変えることができた。
dialogue.local: By placing a wire mesh grid between the heated cathode and the plate, he could control the flow of electricity, turning faint currents into strong, usable signals.
dialogue.en: By placing a wire mesh grid between the heated cathode and the plate, he could control the flow of electricity, turning faint currents into strong, usable signals.

dialogue.text: Triodes transformed communication.
dialogue.zh: 三極管改變了通訊方式。
dialogue.ja: トライオードは通信を変革した。
dialogue.local: Triodes transformed communication.
dialogue.en: Triodes transformed communication.

dialogue.text: They gave birth to the modern radio, enabled long distance telephony, and connected continents.
dialogue.zh: 它們催生了現代無線電，實現了長距離電話，連接了大陸。
dialogue.ja: それらは現代のラジオを生み出し、長距離電話を可能にし、大陸を繋いだ。
dialogue.local: They gave birth to the modern radio, enabled long distance telephony, and connected continents.
dialogue.en: They gave birth to the modern radio, enabled long distance telephony, and connected continents.

dialogue.text: A small change of the grid could regulate a much larger current between cathode and plate, a principle that was truly revolutionary.
dialogue.zh: 柵極的小幅調整能控制陰極與金屬板間的大電流，這原理極具革命性。
dialogue.ja: グリッドの小さな変化が陰極とプレート間の大きな電流を調整できるという原理は、まさに革命的だった。
dialogue.local: A small change of the grid could regulate a much larger current between cathode and plate, a principle that was truly revolutionary.
dialogue.en: A small change of the grid could regulate a much larger current between cathode and plate, a principle that was truly revolutionary.

dialogue.text: Yet these early tubes remained fragile, bulky, and power-hungry.
dialogue.zh: 然而這些早期真空管仍然脆弱、笨重且耗電。
dialogue.ja: しかし、これらの初期の真空管は依然として壊れやすく、大きくて電力を大量に消費した。
dialogue.local: Yet these early tubes remained fragile, bulky, and power-hungry.
dialogue.en: Yet these early tubes remained fragile, bulky, and power-hungry.

dialogue.text: By the 1940s, the promise of electronic amplification had grown into something huge.
dialogue.zh: 到了1940年代，電子放大的潛力已成為巨大力量。
dialogue.ja: 1940年代までに、電子増幅の可能性は巨大なものへと成長していた。
dialogue.local: By the 1940s, the promise of electronic amplification had grown into something huge.
dialogue.en: By the 1940s, the promise of electronic amplification had grown into something huge.

dialogue.text: Things like the electronic numerical integrator and computer relied on tens of thousands of vacuum tubes to perform calculations, filling entire rooms with blinking panels and glowing filaments.
dialogue.zh: 電子數值積分器和電腦等設備依賴數萬個真空管進行計算，整個房間充滿閃爍的面板和發光的燈絲。
dialogue.ja: 電子数値積分器やコンピューターは数万本の真空管を使って計算を行い、部屋中が点滅するパネルと光るフィラメントで満たされていた。
dialogue.local: Things like the electronic numerical integrator and computer relied on tens of thousands of vacuum tubes to perform calculations, filling entire rooms with blinking panels and glowing filaments.
dialogue.en: Things like the electronic numerical integrator and computer relied on tens of thousands of vacuum tubes to perform calculations, filling entire rooms with blinking panels and glowing filaments.

dialogue.text: These power-hungry machines consumed massive amounts of electricity and required constant maintenance, as tubes frequently burned out or failed.
dialogue.zh: 這些耗電巨大的機器消耗大量電力，且需不斷維護，因為真空管經常燒壞或故障。
dialogue.ja: これらの電力を大量に消費する機械は頻繁に真空管が切れたり故障したりするため、常にメンテナンスが必要だった。
dialogue.local: These power-hungry machines consumed massive amounts of electricity and required constant maintenance, as tubes frequently burned out or failed.
dialogue.en: These power-hungry machines consumed massive amounts of electricity and required constant maintenance, as tubes frequently burned out or failed.

dialogue.text: Computers were searching for something smaller and far more reliable.
dialogue.zh: 電腦尋找更小且更可靠的元件。
dialogue.ja: コンピューターはより小さく、はるかに信頼性の高いものを求めていた。
dialogue.local: Computers were searching for something smaller and far more reliable.
dialogue.en: Computers were searching for something smaller and far more reliable.

dialogue.text: At Bell Telephone Laboratories, John Bardeen, Walter Brittain, and William Shockley developed a new kind of amplifier, the transistor.
dialogue.zh: 在貝爾電話實驗室，約翰·巴丁、沃爾特·布萊坦和威廉·肖克利開發了一種新型放大器——晶體管。
dialogue.ja: ベル電話研究所で、ジョン・バーディーン、ウォルター・ブラッテン、ウィリアム・ショックレーが新しいタイプの増幅器、トランジスタを開発した。
dialogue.local: At Bell Telephone Laboratories, John Bardeen, Walter Brittain, and William Shockley developed a new kind of amplifier, the transistor.
dialogue.en: At Bell Telephone Laboratories, John Bardeen, Walter Brittain, and William Shockley developed a new kind of amplifier, the transistor.

dialogue.text: The transistor, operating on a new and different principle, arising from basic research on solid substances and how the electrons inside them behave, investigating the surface properties of germanium, a substance known to be a semiconductor of electricity, their studies suggested a way to amplify an electric current within a solid.
dialogue.zh: 晶體管基於一種全新原理，源自對固體物質及其內部電子行為的基礎研究，研究了已知為半導體的鍺的表面特性，提出了在固體內放大電流的方法。
dialogue.ja: トランジスタは新しく異なる原理で動作し、固体物質とその中の電子の挙動に関する基礎研究から生まれた。電気の半導体として知られるゲルマニウムの表面特性を調査し、固体内で電流を増幅する方法を示唆した。
dialogue.local: The transistor, operating on a new and different principle, arising from basic research on solid substances and how the electrons inside them behave, investigating the surface properties of germanium, a substance known to be a semiconductor of electricity, their studies suggested a way to amplify an electric current within a solid.
dialogue.en: The transistor, operating on a new and different principle, arising from basic research on solid substances and how the electrons inside them behave, investigating the surface properties of germanium, a substance known to be a semiconductor of electricity, their studies suggested a way to amplify an electric current within a solid.

dialogue.text: The transistor was born.
dialogue.zh: 晶體管誕生了。
dialogue.ja: トランジスタが誕生した。
dialogue.local: The transistor was born.
dialogue.en: The transistor was born.

dialogue.text: Bell Labs coined the name transistor, combining transconductance and varister.
dialogue.zh: 貝爾實驗室創造了「transistor」這個名稱，結合了跨導和變阻器兩詞。
dialogue.ja: ベル研究所は「トランジスタ」という名前を作り出した。これはトランスコンダクタンスとバリスターを組み合わせたものだ。
dialogue.local: Bell Labs coined the name transistor, combining transconductance and varister.
dialogue.en: Bell Labs coined the name transistor, combining transconductance and varister.

dialogue.text: Other proposed names included the semiconductor triode.
dialogue.zh: 其他提議的名稱包括半導體三極管。
dialogue.ja: 他に提案された名前には半導体トライオードがあった。
dialogue.local: Other proposed names included the semiconductor triode.
dialogue.en: Other proposed names included the semiconductor triode.

dialogue.text: In 1947, they unveiled the first working prototype, a PNP point contact transistor made from germanium instead of vacuum tubes.
dialogue.zh: 1947年，他們展示了第一個可用的原型，是用鍺製成的PNP點接觸型晶體管，取代了真空管。
dialogue.ja: 1947年、彼らは真空管の代わりにゲルマニウムで作られたPNPポイントコンタクトトランジスタの最初の動作試作機を発表した。
dialogue.local: In 1947, they unveiled the first working prototype, a PNP point contact transistor made from germanium instead of vacuum tubes.
dialogue.en: In 1947, they unveiled the first working prototype, a PNP point contact transistor made from germanium instead of vacuum tubes.

dialogue.text: This is one of the latest transistors, a much more sophisticated device, but based on the same physical principles as its ancestor.
dialogue.zh: 這是其中一款最新的晶體管，功能更先進，但基於與其祖先相同的物理原理。
dialogue.ja: これは最新のトランジスタの一つで、はるかに高度な装置だが、先祖と同じ物理原理に基づいている。
dialogue.local: This is one of the latest transistors, a much more sophisticated device, but based on the same physical principles as its ancestor.
dialogue.en: This is one of the latest transistors, a much more sophisticated device, but based on the same physical principles as its ancestor.

dialogue.text: The impact of the transistor on the electronic industry and on our society is unquestioned.
dialogue.zh: 晶體管對電子產業及社會的影響無可置疑。
dialogue.ja: トランジスタが電子産業と社会に与えた影響は疑いようがない。
dialogue.local: The impact of the transistor on the electronic industry and on our society is unquestioned.
dialogue.en: The impact of the transistor on the electronic industry and on our society is unquestioned.

dialogue.text: Their transistor worked on a principle similar to the triode.
dialogue.zh: 他們的晶體管運作原理類似於三極管。
dialogue.ja: 彼らのトランジスタはトライオードに似た原理で動作した。
dialogue.local: Their transistor worked on a principle similar to the triode.
dialogue.en: Their transistor worked on a principle similar to the triode.

dialogue.text: A small input of the transistor's base could control a much larger current flowing between the emitter and collector contacts of the germanium crystal.
dialogue.zh: 晶體管基座的小電流能控制鍺晶體中發射極與集電極間的大電流。
dialogue.ja: トランジスタのベースへの小さな入力が、ゲルマニウム結晶のエミッターとコレクター間の大きな電流を制御できた。
dialogue.local: A small input of the transistor's base could control a much larger current flowing between the emitter and collector contacts of the germanium crystal.
dialogue.en: A small input of the transistor's base could control a much larger current flowing between the emitter and collector contacts of the germanium crystal.

dialogue.text: In essence, the transistor was a solid state triode.
dialogue.zh: 本質上，晶體管是一種固態三極管。
dialogue.ja: 本質的に、トランジスタは固体状態のトライオードだった。
dialogue.local: In essence, the transistor was a solid state triode.
dialogue.en: In essence, the transistor was a solid state triode.

dialogue.text: The analogy to the triode's grid made its operation easier to understand, but now it was solid state, without the heat, bulk, or fragility of vacuum tubes, and without filaments to burn out.
dialogue.zh: 類比三極管的柵極使其操作更易理解，但它是固態的，沒有真空管的熱量、笨重和脆弱，也沒有燈絲會燒壞。
dialogue.ja: トライオードのグリッドとの類似性で動作が理解しやすくなったが、今や固体状態であり、真空管の熱さやかさばり、壊れやすさもなく、フィラメントの焼き切れもなかった。
dialogue.local: The analogy to the triode's grid made its operation easier to understand, but now it was solid state, without the heat, bulk, or fragility of vacuum tubes, and without filaments to burn out.
dialogue.en: The analogy to the triode's grid made its operation easier to understand, but now it was solid state, without the heat, bulk, or fragility of vacuum tubes, and without filaments to burn out.

dialogue.text: The three inventors were later awarded the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.
dialogue.zh: 這三位發明家後來獲得1956年諾貝爾物理學獎。
dialogue.ja: この三人の発明者は後に1956年にノーベル物理学賞を受賞した。
dialogue.local: The three inventors were later awarded the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.
dialogue.en: The three inventors were later awarded the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.

dialogue.text: The invention of the transistor revolutionized computing.
dialogue.zh: 晶體管的發明徹底改變了計算機領域。
dialogue.ja: トランジスタの発明はコンピューターを革命的に変えた。
dialogue.local: The invention of the transistor revolutionized computing.
dialogue.en: The invention of the transistor revolutionized computing.

dialogue.text: By the late 1950s, transistors had moved beyond the laboratory.
dialogue.zh: 到了1950年代末，晶體管已走出實驗室。
dialogue.ja: 1950年代後半までに、トランジスタは研究室の外に出ていた。
dialogue.local: By the late 1950s, transistors had moved beyond the laboratory.
dialogue.en: By the late 1950s, transistors had moved beyond the laboratory.

dialogue.text: Engineers began replacing bulky vacuum tubes with transistors, creating machines that were faster, more compact, and far more reliable.
dialogue.zh: 工程師開始用晶體管取代笨重的真空管，打造更快、更小巧且更可靠的機器。
dialogue.ja: 技術者たちはかさばる真空管をトランジスタに置き換え、より速く、よりコンパクトで、はるかに信頼性の高い機械を作り始めた。
dialogue.local: Engineers began replacing bulky vacuum tubes with transistors, creating machines that were faster, more compact, and far more reliable.
dialogue.en: Engineers began replacing bulky vacuum tubes with transistors, creating machines that were faster, more compact, and far more reliable.

dialogue.text: One landmark example was the IBM 7090, a fully transistorized computer introduced in 1959.
dialogue.zh: 一個里程碑式的例子是1959年推出的全晶體管電腦IBM 7090。
dialogue.ja: 画期的な例として、1959年に導入された完全トランジスタ化コンピューターのIBM 7090がある。
dialogue.local: One landmark example was the IBM 7090, a fully transistorized computer introduced in 1959.
dialogue.en: One landmark example was the IBM 7090, a fully transistorized computer introduced in 1959.

dialogue.text: The IBM 7090 played a crucial role in space exploration.
dialogue.zh: IBM 7090在太空探索中扮演了關鍵角色。
dialogue.ja: IBM 7090は宇宙探査で重要な役割を果たした。
dialogue.local: The IBM 7090 played a crucial role in space exploration.
dialogue.en: The IBM 7090 played a crucial role in space exploration.

dialogue.text: NASA used it to perform the complex calculations needed to plan trajectories and guidance systems for missions that would eventually take humans to the moon.
dialogue.zh: NASA使用它進行複雜計算，規劃軌跡與導航系統，支持最終將人類送上月球的任務。
dialogue.ja: NASAはこれを使って軌道や誘導システムの複雑な計算を行い、最終的に人類を月に送るミッションを計画した。
dialogue.local: NASA used it to perform the complex calculations needed to plan trajectories and guidance systems for missions that would eventually take humans to the moon.
dialogue.en: NASA used it to perform the complex calculations needed to plan trajectories and guidance systems for missions that would eventually take humans to the moon.

dialogue.text: This is the Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland.
dialogue.zh: 這是位於馬里蘭州格林貝爾特的高達太空飛行中心。
dialogue.ja: ここはメリーランド州グリーンベルトにあるゴダード宇宙飛行センターだ。
dialogue.local: This is the Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland.
dialogue.en: This is the Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland.

dialogue.text: Through here, follows the voice and teletype communications that linked the global stations to mercury control.
dialogue.zh: 這裡傳送著連接全球站點與水星計劃控制中心的語音和電傳通訊。
dialogue.ja: ここを通じて、世界中の基地とマーキュリー管制を結ぶ音声とテレタイプ通信が行われている。
dialogue.local: Through here, follows the voice and teletype communications that linked the global stations to mercury control.
dialogue.en: Through here, follows the voice and teletype communications that linked the global stations to mercury control.

dialogue.text: The computers enable men to reach judgments within the flashes of time allowed for control of the spacecraft that moves faster than a brain can react.
dialogue.zh: 電腦使人們能在極短時間內做出判斷，控制比大腦反應還快的太空船。
dialogue.ja: コンピューターは、人間の脳の反応よりも速く動く宇宙船の制御に必要な短時間で判断を下せるようにした。
dialogue.local: The computers enable men to reach judgments within the flashes of time allowed for control of the spacecraft that moves faster than a brain can react.
dialogue.en: The computers enable men to reach judgments within the flashes of time allowed for control of the spacecraft that moves faster than a brain can react.

dialogue.text: Throughout the flight, the computers will generate recommendations on whether the mission should continue or be aborted.
dialogue.zh: 整個飛行過程中，電腦會生成建議，判斷任務是否繼續或中止。
dialogue.ja: 飛行中ずっと、コンピューターはミッションを続行すべきか中止すべきかの提案を出す。
dialogue.local: Throughout the flight, the computers will generate recommendations on whether the mission should continue or be aborted.
dialogue.en: Throughout the flight, the computers will generate recommendations on whether the mission should continue or be aborted.

dialogue.text: They will determine locations of the spacecraft.
dialogue.zh: 它們會確定太空船的位置。
dialogue.ja: 宇宙船の位置を特定する。
dialogue.local: They will determine locations of the spacecraft.
dialogue.en: They will determine locations of the spacecraft.

dialogue.text: The time it should begin re-entry, the point at which it will end.
dialogue.zh: 何時開始再入大氣層，以及再入結束的時間點。
dialogue.ja: 再突入を開始すべき時刻と、その終了地点を決定する。
dialogue.local: The time it should begin re-entry, the point at which it will end.
dialogue.en: The time it should begin re-entry, the point at which it will end.

dialogue.text: Today is February 20, 1962, and today, if all goes well, the men here will launch an American astronaut in the orbit around the world in a spacecraft which he has named, Friendship 7.
dialogue.zh: 今天是1962年2月20日，如果一切順利，這裡的人將發射一位美國太空人在名為友誼7號的太空船中繞地球軌道飛行。
dialogue.ja: 今日は1962年2月20日。すべてが順調なら、ここにいる人々はアメリカの宇宙飛行士をフレンドシップ7号という宇宙船で地球の軌道に打ち上げる。
dialogue.local: Today is February 20, 1962, and today, if all goes well, the men here will launch an American astronaut in the orbit around the world in a spacecraft which he has named, Friendship 7.
dialogue.en: Today is February 20, 1962, and today, if all goes well, the men here will launch an American astronaut in the orbit around the world in a spacecraft which he has named, Friendship 7.

dialogue.text: Friendship 7 awaits its pilot.
dialogue.zh: 友誼7號正在等待它的駕駛員。
dialogue.ja: フレンドシップ7号は操縦士を待っている。
dialogue.local: Friendship 7 awaits its pilot.
dialogue.en: Friendship 7 awaits its pilot.

dialogue.text: His name is John Glenn.
dialogue.zh: 他的名字是約翰·格倫。
dialogue.ja: 操縦士の名前はジョン・グレンだ。
dialogue.local: His name is John Glenn.
dialogue.en: His name is John Glenn.

dialogue.text: All reporters do fast, team out as 18 seconds, and counting engines start.
dialogue.zh: 所有記者準備，倒數18秒，發動機啟動。
dialogue.ja: 全ての記者は準備を、18秒前からカウントダウン、エンジン始動。
dialogue.local: All reporters do fast, team out as 18 seconds, and counting engines start.
dialogue.en: All reporters do fast, team out as 18 seconds, and counting engines start.

dialogue.text: Good Lord, ride all the way.
dialogue.zh: 願上帝保佑，順利飛行。
dialogue.ja: 神よ、どうか無事に飛行させてください。
dialogue.local: Good Lord, ride all the way.
dialogue.en: Good Lord, ride all the way.

dialogue.text: Just run your back up clock, get started.
dialogue.zh: 啟動備用計時器，開始。
dialogue.ja: バックアップクロックを動かして、始めよう。
dialogue.local: Just run your back up clock, get started.
dialogue.en: Just run your back up clock, get started.

dialogue.text: Oh, that view is tremendous.
dialogue.zh: 哦，那景色真壯觀。
dialogue.ja: ああ、その景色は素晴らしい。
dialogue.local: Oh, that view is tremendous.
dialogue.en: Oh, that view is tremendous.

dialogue.text: To John Glenn, now belongs an awesome panorama.
dialogue.zh: 約翰·格倫現在擁有壯麗的全景。
dialogue.ja: ジョン・グレンには今、素晴らしいパノラマが広がっている。
dialogue.local: To John Glenn, now belongs an awesome panorama.
dialogue.en: To John Glenn, now belongs an awesome panorama.

dialogue.text: The world curving beneath him, just as the with film of an earlier Mercury capsule.
dialogue.zh: 世界在他腳下彎曲，就像早期水星太空艙的影像一樣。
dialogue.ja: 彼の下に地球が曲がって見え、まるで以前のマーキュリー宇宙船の映像のようだ。
dialogue.local: The world curving beneath him, just as the with film of an earlier Mercury capsule.
dialogue.en: The world curving beneath him, just as the with film of an earlier Mercury capsule.

dialogue.text: By the 1960s, transistors had become the foundation of modern electronics,
dialogue.zh: 到了1960年代，晶體管已成為現代電子學的基礎，
dialogue.ja: 1960年代までに、トランジスタは現代電子工学の基盤となった。
dialogue.local: By the 1960s, transistors had become the foundation of modern electronics,
dialogue.en: By the 1960s, transistors had become the foundation of modern electronics,

dialogue.text: but the transistors' greatest promise lay in its destiny to shrink.
dialogue.zh: 但晶體管最大的潛力在於它將變得更小。
dialogue.ja: しかし、トランジスタの最大の可能性は小型化にあった。
dialogue.local: but the transistors' greatest promise lay in its destiny to shrink.
dialogue.en: but the transistors' greatest promise lay in its destiny to shrink.

dialogue.text: Engineers soon learned to carve not one, but millions of transistors into a single piece of silicon semiconductor.
dialogue.zh: 工程師很快學會在一塊矽半導體上刻劃不只一個，而是數百萬個晶體管。
dialogue.ja: 技術者たちはすぐに、一つではなく、数百万ものトランジスタを一つのシリコン半導体に刻み込む方法を学んだ。
dialogue.local: Engineers soon learned to carve not one, but millions of transistors into a single piece of silicon semiconductor.
dialogue.en: Engineers soon learned to carve not one, but millions of transistors into a single piece of silicon semiconductor.

dialogue.text: From these integrated circuits, the future of computing was born.
dialogue.zh: 從這些積體電路中，計算的未來誕生了。
dialogue.ja: これらの集積回路から、コンピューティングの未来が生まれた。
dialogue.local: From these integrated circuits, the future of computing was born.
dialogue.en: From these integrated circuits, the future of computing was born.

dialogue.text: What began as a quirk in Edison's light bulb now pulses at the heart of every electronic device we use.
dialogue.zh: 起初只是愛迪生燈泡中的一個奇特現象，現在卻跳動在我們每個電子裝置的核心。
dialogue.ja: エジソンの電球の中の奇妙な現象として始まったものが、今や私たちが使うすべての電子機器の中心で脈打っている。
dialogue.local: What began as a quirk in Edison's light bulb now pulses at the heart of every electronic device we use.
dialogue.en: What began as a quirk in Edison's light bulb now pulses at the heart of every electronic device we use.
